title.narrative: VESP OFF GRANT FOR VOCATIONAL EDUCATION

description.narrative: AVSI Foundation is an international NGO working in 80 districts in Uganda, lead implementing partner for Embassy of Ireland Vocational Education and Skilling Program in Karamoja (VESP). The primary goal of the programme is to increase gainful employment opportunities for 3,500 youth, 50% of whom are female. VESP aims are to (a) Expand youth employment opportunities. (b) Strengthen the capacity of vocational training institutions (VTIs), civil society organizations (CSOs), and the private sector to support skilling and employment and (c) Contribute to the improvement of the legal and policy environment for youth skilling. The programme targets youth across the entire Karamoja region, with a particular focus on Moroto, Nakapiripirit, and Kotido districts. AVSI, is working in partnership with the Karamoja based Institute for International Cooperation and Development (C&D) collaborates with Ministry of Education and Sports, and the selected District authorities in Karamoja, to deliver quality training and skills to over 3,500 youth in the sub-region. This project aims to address the persistent skills gaps (both the supply and demand) in Karamoja, using relevant and attractive vocational training and skilling strategies for the target Karamojong youth. The intervention aims to overcome sociological barriers preventing adolescent girls and boys from entering VTIs and getting relevant skills. AVSI strongly considers disability inclusion in its targeting and selection of the youth with disability for both formal and modular based training, and continues to provide accommodative devices and follow-up of youth with disabilities.
